extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and computational social scientists studying media selection bias and large-scale news analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Represent and discover media selection biases at corpus scale by comparing how news sources mention entities; learn unsupervised, entity-centric representations of topic-specific content selection preferences and use distributional divergence to characterize ideological polarity among sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic representation via named entities (entity pairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent the topic of a text segment by the named entities it mentions, using pairs of entities (two per sentence) to provide focused and finer-grained topic guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use entity pairs to align statements across sources; two entities per sentence are preferred over one for finer-grained topical alignment and context (paper: "We use two instead one, as we observe two entities in a sentence would provide focused and much finer-grained topic guidance").

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity extraction and linking to form topic set
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NER (spaCy en_core_web_sm) to detect mentions, then disambiguate via a simple Wikipedia-based linking method (take title with highest P(t|m)); compute entity frequencies in the corpus and select the top entities as topics (paper uses top 1,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses a small spaCy NER model and the Ratinov et al. (2011) conditional-probability linking heuristic; for a large corpus, selecting the most frequent entities (e.g., 1,000) provides the topic vocabulary for downstream analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context sentence definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define context sentences Cs_e1,e2 as all sentences from a given source that contain mentions of both target entities e1 and e2 within the sample time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only sentences mentioning both entities are considered to represent the source's statements about that entity pair; per-source sets of such sentences are the basis for representing selection preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity-agnostic masking and representation tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: Mask entity mentions with a special token '[ENT]' and insert special relation tokens '[R1]' and '[R2]' after the masks; use the token embeddings of '[R1]' and '[R2]' to jointly represent the context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This design aims to capture topical context while being agnostic to the entity surface forms. The last hidden layers hR1 and hR2 are concatenated and linearly projected to obtain r(c): r(c) = W^T [hR1, hR2].

rubrics_metrics.name: Context sentence encoder architecture (RoBERTa-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize encoder with pretrained RoBERTa-base and fine-tune an encoder that maps masked context sentences to embeddings representing topical context of entity pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper implements encoder using Huggingface transformers, initializes from roberta-base, and constructs embeddings from the special relation token hidden states followed by a linear projection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsupervised training objective: triplet margin loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Train the encoder with a triplet margin loss: for an anchor context sentence c (for entity pair e1,e2), sample a positive sentence c+ from the same entity-pair set and a negative sentence c- that mentions at least one other entity; objective: maximize similarity of anchor-positive relative to anchor-negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use L2 distance and margin (paper: L = max[d(c,c+) - d(c,c-) + 1, 0]). Training data sampled from Wikipedia sentences with two+ mentions of the topic entities (≈3M sentences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data source for encoder
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Wikipedia sentences that contain two or more mentions of the entities of interest to build large-scale unsupervised training data for the triplet objective (paper used ~3M sentences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling from Wikipedia provides coverages of entity co-mentions needed to train an entity-agnostic contextual encoder; ensure sufficient variety of contexts per entity pair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-source, per-entity-pair embedding aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain a source's representation for an entity pair g(Cs_ei,ej) by running each context sentence c ∈ Cs_ei,ej through the encoder and mean-pooling (averaging) the sentence embeddings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mean-pooling across all context sentence embeddings from a source for that entity pair yields the collective content selection preference representation for that source-topic pair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing full source representation via concatenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Form a per-source feature vector by concatenating the source's embeddings for a chosen set of k entity pairs (paper uses k = 20 most frequent entity pairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concatenated embeddings across multiple entity pairs are used as input features for downstream classifiers that predict source-level attributes (e.g., political bias). Choice of k trades off coverage vs sparsity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archetypical entity-pair identification via distributional divergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify Archetypical Entity Pairs (AEPs) that best indicate ideological divide by computing distributional divergence between left- and right-leaning sources' embeddings for each entity pair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit multivariate Gaussians N_L(µL,ΣL) and N_R(µR,ΣR) to left- and right-leaning source embeddings for each entity pair and compute two-way KL divergence: D(NL||NR) = 1/2 (tr(Σ_R^{-1} Σ_L) + ln(|Σ_R|/|Σ_L|) + (µR-µL)^T Σ_R^{-1} (µR-µL) - d). Rank entity pairs by D to select AEPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using distributional divergence as indicator of ideological polarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the distributional divergence (KL between fitted Gaussians) of per-source embeddings for an entity pair as a measure of how indicative that pair is of left-vs-right ideological differences among sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entity pairs with higher D(NL||NR) are better indicators; compute divergence for many frequent pairs (paper computed for 100 most frequent) and select top-N as archetypical pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polarity prediction setup and evaluation labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate ideologic polarity prediction as a three-way {left, center, right} classification by aggregating five-way bias labels (AllSides and MBFC) into three classes; train on AllSides and evaluate on MBFC-held-out sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove overlap between training and test label sets; verify label agreement between label sources (paper reports 81.99 weighted macro F1 between AllSides and MBFC on overlap).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classifier choices and hyperparameter tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use small-capacity classifiers (Lasso, Ridge, Linear SVM, RBF-kernel SVM) on frozen embeddings; select hyperparameters by 5-fold cross-validation on the training set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper reports specific hyperparameters: Lasso C=1; Ridge α=1.0; Linear SVM C=0.1 L2 hinge; RBF SVM C=2 γ=0.01 degree=3. Use cross-validation to avoid overfitting and freeze embeddings during classifier training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline comparison with unfine-tuned pretrained encoder
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare proposed encoder (trained with the triplet objective) against RoBERTa-base embeddings without fine-tuning to evaluate the benefit of the task-specific representation learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use same downstream classifiers and features selection (k entity pairs) for fair comparison; paper reports consistent improvements over RoBERTa except for one baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for polarity prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: Report weighted macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1 (F_{β=1}) for the three-way polarity classification task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use held-out test set (MBFC sources not in AllSides) and 5-fold CV on AllSides for hyperparameter selection; report P, R, F as in Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization and qualitative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PCA visualization of per-source embeddings for representative entity pairs to inspect topic variance and left-vs-right divergence; interpret PCA plots for qualitative insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCA of source representations per-entity-pair can reveal scatteredness (topic variance) and clustering/divergence aligned with ideological labels; use illustrative examples (e.g., U.S. House & Senate vs Russia & United States).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probing contextual embeddings with subjective predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: Project context sentence embeddings onto subjective verb predicate embeddings (from MPQA lexicon) to infer sentiment/polarity expressed in contexts per source and entity pair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct 400 verb predicate prompts (200 most frequent positive and negative), encode them with the same encoder, compute cosine similarity to a context embedding, take top-10 predicates and weighted mean of their polarity labels (positive=1, negative=-1) via softmax over similarities to yield a sentiment score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and coverage constraint for detecting selection bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare statements made by different sources on the same topics within a relatively small time frame to reduce confounding due to time-varying coverage; focus only on topics both/all sources cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methodology adopts the 'same-topic-same-timeframe' comparison strategy (as opposed to presence/absence observations) because it better reflects diverging framing choices; the study intentionally leaves partial-coverage cases (where sources don't both cover a topic) for future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sufficiency and limitation considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Method requires large amounts of unlabeled data and sufficient counts of context sentences per entity pair; sparse entity-pair coverage can limit analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly acknowledge limitations: need enough presence of context sentences per entity pair, focus on shared topics across sources, and results are exploratory/speculative rather than definitive evidence of bias.
